baer-heitev/1:א: (א) Shavuot. See Magen Avraham in what he wrote that according to all opinions the Torah was given on the 51st day of counting — why did the Holy One, blessed be He, establish the festival of Shavuot for generations on the 50th day of counting before and after noon. And Maharsha in ch. 1 ch. 1 of Avodah Zarah in the sugya "Heaven and earth testify regarding their testimony" etc. also raised this question and answered there that the Holy One, blessed be He, intended thereby to teach that fear of sin precedes wisdom in rank and in time before noon. And according to this I said that this is the intention of Rav Yosef, that on Yom Tov of Shavuot they made him a three-year-old calf; he said: if not for this day that causes it, how many Josephs are in the market — end of his words; see Pesachim 68a. It is fitting to examine it well. First, what is this language that he says "if not for this day that causes" — it implies the day causes it; he should have said "if not for the giving of the Torah." And further, if not for the giving of the Torah the world would return to void and formlessness, as we say in the baraita: the Holy One, blessed be He, with the act of Creation — if Israel accept the Torah, good; if not, I will return them to void and formlessness. And further, after Rav Yosef was the most humble of any person as we say at the end of Sotah — when Rabbi died humility ceased, Rav Yosef said to him: do not teach humility for I am here before noon — and here he boasts that because of the giving of the Torah he is superior to other people; this is not within the bounds of humility. And according to what I wrote, his intention was thus in what he said "if not for this day" etc., for it is known what Chazal said: humility brings to fear of sin. If so, Rav Yosef was on a level in that he was humble, he was also on a level that his fear of sin preceded his wisdom. And this is what he said on Yom Tov of Shavuot — meaning on the 50th day they made him a three-year-old calf and he said: if not for this day that causes — meaning if the day of Shavuot were not on this day but on the 51st day of counting, it would not be proven that fear of sin precedes wisdom in rank and in time, and my superiority would be nothing, and how many Josephs are in the market; but now that the day of Shavuot is on the 50th day and the giving of the Torah was on the 51st day, the question is difficult and must be answered as Maharsha wrote, and understand well. And the later authorities wrote that they delay Ma'ariv at the entry of Shavuot so that the days of counting shall be complete.

mechaber/1:main: The fiftieth day of the count of the Omer is the holiday of Shavuot. The prayer service is like the holiday of Passover, rather we say "the Holiday of Shavuot, the time of the giving of our Torah". We say full Hallel. We take out two Torah scrolls and read in the first one of five [sections] from "The third month" until the end of the order. The Maftir is read in the second scroll, "On the day of the first fruits". As Haftorah we read the chariot of Ezekiel, and end with the verse "and the wind took me up."
mechaber/2:main: On the second day, we sing in Parshat Kul Bakur until the end of the Sidra and read a mattir like yesterday and a mattir in Habakkuk from the the Master in his holy temple until the conductor in my music:
mechaber/3:main: It is prohibited to fast immediately after the holiday of Shavuot. {Rama: Rem"a: And we do not say Tachanun from the beginning of Rosh Chodesh Sivan until the 8th day, which is after the post-holiday day (Hagahot Maimoni, Hil' Tefillah Umnagim}. We have the custom to spread out plants on Shavuot in the synagogue and in houses, as a memory for the happiness of the receiving of the Torah. We have a custom everywhere to eat dairy food on the first day of Shavuot. And it seems to me that the reason is: It is like the two foods that are taken on the evening of Pesach, a reminder of the Korban Pesach and a reminder of the Korban Chagiga, so too we eat a dairy food followed by a meat food, and we bring with them two loaves on the table in place of the Mizbeach, and thus there will be a reminder of the two loaves that were brought on "The day of the Bikkurim."}
